headline: Approved site plans for a vehicle repair facility at 10 North Southwood Drive and a 48-unit building at 181 East Hollis Street.
summary: The board approved a vehicle repair facility at 10 North Southwood Drive, a 48-unit building at 181 East Hollis Street, and a flex building on Daniel Webster Highway, each with waivers or conditions. It also extended the approvals for a 9-unit building at 4 Beard Street to October 19, 2028.
decisions: Approved the minutes as amended, 6-0-2, with Bollinger and Green abstaining.
Approved site plan A26-0187 for a vehicle repair facility at 10 North Southwood Drive, with conditions, 8-0.
Approved extension of conditional use permit A26-0204 for 4 Beard Street to October 19, 2028, with no conditions.
Approved extension of site plan A26-0188 for 4 Beard Street to October 19, 2028, with conditions, 8-0.
Approved two waivers for site plan A26-0198 for a 48,000-sqft flex building on Daniel Webster Highway, 8-0.
Approved site plan for a flex building on Daniel Webster Highway, recorded as A26-0188, with 15 conditions, 8-0.
Approved a waiver for site plan A26-0155 at 181 East Hollis Street, 8-0.
Approved a floor area ratio of 2.1 and a 70-foot cumulative driveway width across three curb cuts for site plan A26-0155 at 181 East Hollis Street, 8-0.
Approved site plan A26-0155 for a 48-unit apartment building at 181 East Hollis Street, with conditions, 8-0.
Determined there are no items of regional impact, 8-0.

EXPANDED DRAFT MEETING SUMMARY 
THIS IS NOT AN OFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT OF TAPE RECORDED PROCEEDINGS 
THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED OR APPROVED BY THE NCPB 
 
NASHUA CITY PLANNING BOARD 
October 1, 2026 
 
The regularly scheduled meeting of the Nashua City Planning Board 
was held on October 1, 2026 at 7:00PM in the 3 rd floor auditorium 
in City Hall. 
 
Members Present: Joe MacIntyre, Mayor’s Representative 
 Bob Bollinger, Chair 
 Adam Varley, Vice Chair 
 Cameron Green, Clerk 
 Dan Hudson, City Engineer 
 Ald. Patricia Klee 
 Larry Hirsch 
 Benjamin Zoller 
   
Also Present: Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 Connor Muise, Deputy Planning Manager 
 Scott McPhie, Planner I 
  
APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
October 1, 2026 
 
MOTION by Mr. Zoller to approve the minutes, as amended. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0-2 (Bollinger, Green abstained) 
 
COMMUNICATIONS 
 
- A26-0187, 10 North Southwood Dr 
o Revised staff report 
o Fire apparatus overlay added to plan 
- A26-0188, 181 East Hollis St 
o Updated engineering letter 
o Added condition to staff report 
 
REPORT OF CHAIR, COMMITTEE, & LIAISON 
 
None 
 
PROCEDURES OF THE MEETING
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 2 
 
After the legal notice of each conditional, special use permit, 
site plan or subdivision plan is read by the Chair, the Board will 
determine if that the application is complete and ready for the 
Board to take jurisdiction. The public hearing will begin at which 
time the applicant or representative will be given time to present 
an overview and description of their project. The applicant shall 
speak to whether or not they agree with recommended staff 
stipulations. The Board will then have an opportunity to ask 
questions of the applicant or staff. 
 
The Chair will then ask for testimony from the audience. First 
anyone wishing to speak in opposition or with concern to the plan 
may speak. Please come forward to the microphone, state their name 
and address for the record. This would be the time to ask questions 
they may have regarding the plan. Next public testimony will come 
from anyone wishing to speak in favor of the plan. The applicant 
will then be allowed a rebuttal period at which time they shall 
speak to any issues or concerns raised by prior public testimony. 
 
One public member will then be granted an opportunity to speak to 
those issues brought by the applicant during their rebuttal period. 
The Board will then ask any relevant follow-up questions of the 
applicant if need be. 
 
After this is completed the public hearing will end and the Board 
will resume the public meeting at which time the Board will 
deliberate and vote on the application before us. The Board asks 
that both sides keep their remarks to the subject at hand and try 
not to repeat what has already been said. 
 
Above all, the Board wants to be fair to everyone and make the 
best possible decision based on the testimony presented and all 
applicable approval criteria established in the Nashua Revised 
Ordinances for conditional, special use permits, site plans and 
subdivisions. Thank you for your interest and courteous attention. 
Please turn off your cell phones and pagers at this time. 
 
Per our legal charter, we have a quorum when five members are 
present. There may be some recusals this evening for certain board 
members, but as long as five members are sitting each case can be 
heard. At the discretion of the chair, the order of the cases can 
be rearranged.  
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 3 
 
A26-0187  10 North Southwood Drive, LLC (Owner), Wendat, LLC 
(Applicant) requesting Conditional Use Permit approval 
for a vehicle repair and service facility. Property is 
located at 10 North Southwood Drive.  Map G – Lot 591. 
Zoned Park Industrial (PI). Ward 2. 
 
MOTION by Mr. MacIntyre that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Varley 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
Paul Chisholm, Civil Engineer, Keach Nordstrom Associates, 5 
Commerce Park N Ste 201, Bedford, NH 
 
Mr. Chisholm introduced himself on behalf of the applicant, an 
affiliate of Tulley Automotive Group. Tulley is the driving force 
behind this project and they are ultimately going to own and 
operate the site. They are proposing to repurpose this property, 
originally built in 1994 for the Post Office and most recently 
occupied by Waveguide Solutions. The parcel is about 10 acres, 
located in the PI zone and the Water Supply Protection District. 
This is an adaptive reuse of the property to supplement Tulley’s 
existing dealership operations.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said Tulley Automotive Group is a long-established 
Nashua business that experienced a significant amount of growth in 
recent years. In terms of the Land Use Code there are two uses 
contemplated for this site, vehicle storage and vehicle repair. 
Vehicle storage is permitted by right, vehicle repair is permitted 
only by Conditional Use Permit 
 
Mr. Chisholm said Tulley does not intend this site to be a high 
volume, customer centric location. They want customers and 
operations to be running through the main dealership in south 
Nashua. Employees will shuttle vehicles back and forth from the 
dealership to this site. Repair here are going to be the longer-
term projects, things that take multiple days to complete. They 
estimate 75 vehicles a month to be serviced here, 3-4 vehicles per 
day. They will experience some customers coming to the site, but 
to a limited degree. They will have 25 employees onsite.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said the vehicle storage component will act very 
similarly to their property on 131 West Glenwood Street. As 
inventory fluxes they have the ability to store cars there and 
shuttle them between the dealership. This will be the same. This
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 4 
 
site is enticing to them because it is close to the highway, they 
don’t have to go through local roads, there’s tremendous 
infrastructure there.  
 
Mr. Chisholm summarized the nine criteria of a conditional use 
permit, as detailed in the supplemental packet documentation. He 
said the applicant feels this is a great property, they see a lot 
of potential here. They are thinking about what to do in the 
future, there is a potential for expansion in the future. That 
will come back before this Board.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if the intent is to have the access on Tinker 
Road remain gated ? 
 
Mr. Chisholm said correct. There are three access driveways, one 
off Tinker and two off North Southwood. Each of the driveways has 
gated sliding fences. They don’t intend to use the Tinker Road 
access but they intend to keep it for emergency purposes.  
 
Ald. Klee said this is where the old Post Office facility was. The 
vehicles coming in and out of here for Tulley probably aren’t going 
to be more than what was there before.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said correct. Particularly with the Post Office there 
was a lot more traffic. The most recent tenant was a contractor 
with larger utility vehicles. This is a lot less intense of a use 
than what has been there historically.  
 
Ald. Klee asked what the hours of operation are.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said the site will follow the dealership hours. Monday 
through Friday, 7AM-6PM, Saturday 8AM-5Pm, Sunday 11AM-4PM. That’s 
the worst-case scenario, they typically give the service staff 
Sundays off.   
 
Mr. Zoller asked if there are any existing nonconformities on the 
site they are aware of.  
 
Mr. Chisholm said as far as we know the site is compliant, we 
haven’t come across anything we need to fix. We feel there is room 
to expand without triggering relief.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 5 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Bollinger closed the public hearing and moved into the public 
meeting. He said this seems fairly straightforward. He lives in 
the area, you almost wouldn’t know anything was there. He was there 
during the Post Office operations, he would think overall from a 
traffic standpoint he doesn’t see it as a big deal. Otherwise, the 
written and oral testimony are more than satisfactory.  
 
Ald. Klee said she agrees. Knowing that the Post Office was there 
she doesn’t see this as a concern with traffic. Her other concern 
was the toxicity of an automotive repair shop near a water source, 
but everything she’s seen is that it has been cleared and taken 
care of. She has no concerns.  
 
Mr. Hudson said the Engineering memo requested a traffic 
contribution towards the Amherst St corridor. Given the discussion 
and testimony that traffic will not be routed that way, he doesn’t 
feel that it would be appropriate anymore. They go down to the 
Daniel Webster Hwy site, maybe it would be more applicable there. 
He would like to take this under advisement with Deputy City 
Engineer Mark Saunders and Senior Traffic Engineer Wayne Husband. 
He would expect to contribute that to the Daniel Webster Hwy 
corridor instead of the Amherst Street corridor.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he understands the rationale, it’s a salient 
point if it’s meant to be quarter specific. From a procedural 
standpoint, how would we treat that in conditions? 
 
Mr. Hudson said he would modify it to a $9,000 contribution, 
approximately half, towards the Daniel Webster Hwy corridor.  
 
Ald. Klee said we need to leave certain things to the experts, but 
even if they’re going on the highway we still have that 
intersection at Somerset Parkway which could potentially get 
affected. Daniel Webster Hwy is already congested at Exit 3. She 
wouldn’t have a problem with it being transferred, but not reduced. 
The amount of traffic doesn’t hit Amherst St specifically, but it 
will have an impact.
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 6 
 
Mr. Hudson said Somerset Parkway is not part of the Amherst St 
corridor. It is more appropriately directed to DW Hwy, since this 
is a supplementary activity related to that development.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if this is salient to the level of the Planning 
Board or could be handled by the Traffic Dept.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he imagines that this was presented to the 
applicant and agreed to. He’s certain that they wouldn’t complain 
if it were lowered, but he would prefer not to relegate this to 
staff. The crux is one of the subsequent conditions relies on 
satisfying Engineering comments.  
 
Mr. Durfee said he would leave the listed stipulations as is. It 
gives the Engineering Department the flexibility to revise this. 
If the Board feels strongly about a dollar amount they can 
stipulate it, but the intent is to the satisfaction of Engineering 
Dept. If Engineering determines that this is satisfactory, that 
condition is still satisfied.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said in terms of the dollar amount, he would rely on 
staff to devise a proportional fee.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he wanted to know if it rose to the level of 
detail for the Board to be managing the transactional stuff that 
the Traffic Dept. could handle without us getting in their way. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said he thinks Mr. Durfee gave us a path so that we 
don’t have to get into the granular details of exactly how that 
amount is calculated.  
 
Ald. Klee said she doesn’t feel comfortable specifying the dollar 
amount, she would rather that staff make the changes as 
appropriate. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said he thinks the language is broad enough as 
written to accommodate that and give DPW enough latitude to compute 
that in the manner as they see fit.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Varley to approve New Business – Site Plan A26-0187. 
The Board finds that the application meets the Approval Criteria 
under §190-146(D) with the following conditions: 
 
a) Prior to the establishment of the use, all Fire comments shall 
be addressed to the satisfaction of the Fire Marshal’s Office.
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 7 
 
b) Prior to the establishment of the use, all comments from the 
Engineering Department shall be addressed to the satisfaction 
of the Division of Public Works. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Zoller 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
Mr. Bollinger said he would hear A26-0188 and A26-0204 together. 
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS 
A26-0204  Area Agency Properties, Inc. (Owner & Applicant) 
requesting 1-year extension of Conditional Use Permit 
approval of a 3-story, 9-unit multi-family building, 
originally approved on September 5th, 2024, and 
subsequently granted extension on October 16th, 2025. 
Property is located at 4 Beard Street. Map 68 – Lot 148. 
Zoned C Urban Residence (R-C). Ward 3. 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SITE PLANS 
A26-0188  Area Agency Properties, Inc. (Owner & Applicant) 
requesting 1-year extension of site plan approval of a 
3-story, 9-unit multi-family building, originally 
approved on September 5th, 2024, and subsequently 
granted extension on October 16th, 2025. Property is 
located at 4 Beard Street. Map 68 – Lot 148. Zoned C 
Urban Residence (R-C). Ward 3. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the applications are complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
Ethan Beals, Civil Engineer, IMEG Corp, 3 Congress St, Nashua NH 
 
Mr. Beals introduced himself on behalf of the applicant. He said 
this is a second extension of the approval. Area Agency Properties 
does business as Gateways Community Services, a nonprofit who 
provides services including housing for the developmentally 
disabled community. The group home at 4 Beard St has reached the 
end of its usable life and it is being proposed to demolish the 
single-family home and construct a 9-unit residence in its place. 
This is a one of a kind project for the city and the state. It
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 8 
 
will be managed by Gateways and house a mix of clients and staff. 
The plans have not changed since the 2024 approval, we are just 
off to a slower start than we hoped. All of their funds are mostly 
tied to providing services for their clients, they are reliant on 
fundraising to support a project like this. We are very hopeful 
that we are moving in the right direction. Granting an extension 
will allow our clients to continue to work through these various 
funding opportunities and seek other grants for the project.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if this group had a fundraiser last night.  
 
Mr. Beals said no.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he might have been thinking about Front Door 
Agency, his daughter serves on that Board. 
 
Mr. Green asked if they want to consider extending the approval 
for the nonprofit.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said we have seen this on multiple nonprofits 
recently, the funding is a mechanism to break ground, let alone 
the full build. We have exerted that discretion previously. He 
asked if the applicant would object.  
 
Mr. Beals said as much as he appreciates his annual calendar 
reminder to write a check and submit the application, he feels bad 
for staff to see this multiple times. He loves coming to the 
Planning Board meeting but it would go a long way for his clients 
to extend. He is hopeful they will break ground next year but he 
can’t definitively give a construction schedule.  
 
Ald. Klee said she agrees with Mr. Green. If they’re not sure they 
can break ground in the next year, she would like to extend. 
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Bollinger closed the public hearing and moved into the public 
meeting.
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 9 
 
 
Mr. Durfee said that would fine. They can set a date so Mr. Beals 
can set that calendar reminder. That could be October 19, 2028. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said we’re not setting precedent here, given the 
extenuating circumstances with the fundraising. If we can spare a 
nonprofit another application fee it is within our power to do so. 
 
Ald. Klee said she agrees. It would take the burden off the 
applicant. She would not want to go past 2028, she fears that the 
property would languish. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Conditional Use 
Permit A26-0204, to be extended to October 19, 2028. The Board 
finds that the application meets the Approval Criteria under §190-
133(F) with no conditions. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Site Plan A26-0188, 
to be extended to October 19, 2028. The Board finds that the 
application meets the Approval Criteria under §190-146(D) with the 
following conditions: 
 
a. All Previous conditions of approval granted at the October 
16, 2025, Nashua Planning Board meeting are included as 
conditions of this approval.  
 
b. All comments in a letter from Joe Mendola, Senior Staff 
Engineer, dated August 30, 2024, will be addressed to the 
satisfaction of the Department of Public Works. 
 
c. All comments in an email from Jeff Labrie, Fire Inspector 
Investigator, dated September 14, 2026, will be addressed to 
the satisfaction of the Fire Department. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he appreciates the forward thinking of Mr. Green 
to extend this application for two years. He does not empathize 
with Mr. Beals, he is a professional and can handle it. But he 
thinks it is a good idea to extend the approval. 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
Mr. Bollinger said he will hear A26-0198 next.  
 
NEW BUSINESS – SITE PLANS
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 10 
 
A26-0198  John J. Flatley (Owner & Applicant) requesting site plan 
approval for a 48,000-sqft. flex building, with 
associated site improvements. Property is located at L 
Daniel Webster Highway, Innovative Way Extension. Map A 
– Lots 44 & 712. Zoned Park Industrial (PI). Ward 8. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
Dan Barowski, Licensed Land Surveyor, Fieldstone Land Consultants, 
206 Elm St, Milford NH 
 
Mr. Barowski introduced himself on behalf of the applicant. With 
him tonight is Kevin Walker of the John Flatley Company.  
 
Mr. Barowski said we are here to present a site plan for approval 
on lots A-44 and A-712, collectively 21 acres. There will be a 
48,000-sqft flex building. This is the same application that was 
approved November 17, 2022. This approval has lapsed. We had 
secured state approvals, which are still valid. We are seeking the 
same approval for the site plan that was approved previously. We 
have reviewed the staff report and are amenable to the conditions. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said we just had a rather lengthy discussion about 
extensions. You didn’t want to extend so you just reapplied? 
 
Mr. Barowski said no, we had to reapply. The staff comments are 
the same as the one submitted in 2022.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he isn’t trying to give him a hard time, but 
extension is an option in the future.  
 
*Laughter in the audience* 
 
Mr. Bollinger said in terms of the waivers, it doesn’t look like 
there are any outstanding. The survey of adjacent parcels waiver 
is one we see frequently, and the other one is drafting standards. 
Sometimes with these larger parcels, it’s not uncommon for the 
specified scale to gel with the parcel. Most of the members on the 
Board were there at the time and it would appear that there have 
been no changes.
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 11 
 
Mr. Hudson said it’s the same application as before. There is a 
memo from Senior Staff Engineer Mendola that this is the same plan 
as was previously approved. All of the comments were previously 
approved. It’s the same application, we found no reason to find 
differently than we had before.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he doesn’t want to rush this, but it is the 
same. We can ask the applicant to go into the application, he will 
leave it up to the Board.  
 
Mr. Zoller said he remembers somewhat recently that there was 
Flatley application for site plan we approved, there was a loop 
road and a warehouse type flex building. What we’re looking at is 
a dead end extension of a street. How do the two sites play 
together?  
 
Mr. Durfee said the other site plan was to the north. The road 
that would serve this site is an extension of Innovative Way, it 
terminates right around Digital Drive. The loop road is an 
extension from this extension.  
 
Mr. Zoller asked if this section of the road would need to be in 
place for the other site plan to start? 
 
Mr. Durfee said correct.  
 
Mr. Zoller asked if there is a timing and sequencing issue here.  
 
Mr. Durfee said nothing from an approved phasing plan between site 
plans. There is no requirement to be, you would expect the building 
permit for this application to be pulled first.  
 
Kevin Walker, John Flatley Company 
 
Mr. Walker said he wants to clarify how this comes together. The 
portion of this roadway is also shown on the site plan for the 
property to the north. Either one of them could be built. This 
portion of the road can be built to get up to the property to the 
north if they decide to build it first.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if there are any prospective tenants.  
 
Mr. Walker said it’s a bigger sized flex building than what we 
have out there currently. It will be similar to the other ones, 
tenant wise.
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 12 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Bollinger closed the public hearing and moved into the public 
meeting. He said based on the testimony, it is quite literally the 
same thing as approved a few years ago. We still have coverage for 
the impact fees in the stipulations, all the bases are covered. 
This seems relatively straightforward. He doesn’t think the 
waivers are prohibitive.  
 
Ald. Klee asked why they didn’t request an extension when there 
are no changes. 
 
Mr. Durfee said he does not want to speak for the applicant. 
 
Ald. Klee asked if it was the applicant’s choice.  
 
Mr. Durfee said correct.  
 
Ald. Klee said when this road gets extended in time, would the 
dollar amount for impact fees change? 
 
Mr. Hudson said historically we have done $200 per trip, which 
went up to $250 a year ago. There’s been a fairly recent bump. We 
felt the fairest thing was to keep the fee the same as if this was 
an extension we carried forward.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve the following waivers for New 
Business – Site Plan A26-0198: 
 
a. §190-279 (EE): To waive the requirement to show existing 
conditions on ‘adjacent parcels' as appropriate.  
 
b. §190-282(A): To waive certain drafting standards for the plan 
to be no smaller than 50 feet to one inch, 
 
As per RSA 674:36(II)(N), RSA 674:44(III)(e), and §190-148(D), 
Strict conformity would pose an unnecessary hardship to the 
Applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 13 
 
intent of the regulations; and specific circumstances, or 
conditions of the land, and the waiver will properly carry out the 
spirit and intent of the regulations. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Varley 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Site Plan A26-0188. 
The Board finds that the application meets the Approval Criteria 
under §190-146(D) with the following conditions: 
 
a. Any waiver(s) granted shall be listed on the plan. Should any 
waiver(s) be denied, the plan must be revised in order to 
comply with the applicable site plan regulations.  
 
b. All outstanding comments in a memo from Joe Mendola, Senior 
Staff Engineer, dated October 8, 2026, will be addressed to 
the satisfaction of the Division of Public Works.  
 
c. All outstanding comments in an e-mail from Michael DuVarney, 
Fire Marshall, dated October 9, 2026, will be addressed to 
the satisfaction of the Fire Department  
 
d. Prior to the Chair signing the plan, necessary portions of 
Dozer Road and other necessary road rights-of-way shall be 
discontinued through the Board of Aldermen process.  
 
e. Subsequent to the discontinuance of that portion of Dozer 
Road, the final signed plan will add a note and show that 
portion of Dozer Road as discontinued.  
 
f. A lot merger form will be completed and placed on file.  
 
g. All addresses shall be shown on the approved site plan.  
 
h. All technical review comments listed in Section 5 of the 
Planning Board staff report shall be addressed to the 
satisfaction of the Planning Department.  
 
i. The plan shall include a signature and seal of a New Hampshire 
licensed engineer, surveyor, and architect, on applicable 
sheets.  
 
j. Prior to any work being done, a pre-construction meeting with 
the City shall take place.
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 14 
 
 
k. Prior to any work being done, a financial guarantee for all 
off-site improvements shall be approved and submitted to the 
City.  
 
l. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, stormwater 
documents in accordance with §190-217 shall be submitted for 
review by City staff and recorded at the Applicant’s expense.  
 
m. Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, a 
conditional use permit must be approved for Flex use building 
construction in the PI zone. (See§190-215 use #69 in Table 
15-1)  
 
n. Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, all site 
improvements will be completed in accordance with the 
approved plan.  
 
o. Prior to the issuance of the final Certificate of Occupancy, 
an as-built plan locating all driveways, buildings, 
utilities, and site landscaping shall be completed by a 
professional engineer or a licensed land surveyor and 
submitted to the Engineering and Planning Departments. The 
as-built plan shall include a statement that all construction 
was completed in accordance with the approved site plan and 
applicable local regulations. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SITE PLANS 
A26-0155  Datec Tool & Machine, Inc. (Owner), Bolduc Enterprises, 
LLC (Applicant) requesting site plan approval to 
construct a 48-unit multifamily building, with 
associated site improvements. Property is located at 181 
East Hollis Street. Map 50 – Sheet 24. Zoned General 
Industrial / Transit Oriented Development (GI/TOD). Ward 
7. (Postponed to the October 15, 2026 meeting by 
Applicant request) 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Zoller
NCPB 
October 1, 2026 
Page 15 
 
MOTION CARRIED 8-0 
 
Pete Madsen, Civil Engineer, Keach Nordstrom Associates, 5 
Commerce Park N Ste 201, Bedford NH 
 
Mr. Madsen introduced himself on behalf of the applicant. With him 
tonight is Nick Bolduc from Bolduc Enterprises, Paul Chisholm from 
Keach Nordstrom Associates, and architect Tina Walker from
